#----------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
set.seed(42)
num_points <- 150
yrange <- xrange <- c(0, 100)
point_col <- rgb(matrix(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Greys")[5]) / 255, ncol=3), alpha=0.5)
```

```{r}
# create random data
x_rand <- runif(num_points, xrange[1], xrange[2])
y_rand <- runif(num_points, yrange[1], yrange[2])
df_rand <- data.frame(x=x_rand, y=y_rand, type=sample(letters, num_points, rep=T))
# coordinates(df_rand) <- ~ x + y
```

```{r}
# create clustered data
x_clust <- rnorm(num_points, mean=mean(xrange), sd=5)
y_clust <- rnorm(num_points, mean=mean(yrange), sd=5)
df_clust <- data.frame(x=x_clust, y=y_clust, type=sample(letters, num_points, rep=T))
# coordinates(df_clust) <- ~ x + y
```


```{r}
# create uniform data
unif_grid <- expand.grid(1:ceiling(sqrt(num_points)), 1:ceiling(sqrt(num_points))) + matrix(rnorm(ceiling(sqrt(num_points))^2, mean=0, sd=0.3), nrow=ceiling(sqrt(num_points)))
samp <- sample(1:ceiling(sqrt(num_points))^2, num_points)
x_unif <- unif_grid[samp, 1]
y_unif <- unif_grid[samp, 2]
df_unif <- data.frame(x=x_unif, y=y_unif, type=sample(letters, num_points, rep=T))
# coordinates(df_unif) <- ~ x + y
```


```{r}
# do the Ripley's K analysis
set.seed(42)
N <- 100
# test_df <- df_rand
test_df <- df_clust
# test_df <- df_unif
```

```{r}
p <- ppp(test_df$x, test_df$y, owin(range(test_df$x), range(test_df$y)))
# p <- ppp(test_df$x, test_df$y, owin(xrange, yrange))
K <- Kest(p)
L <- sqrt(K$border / pi) - K$r
```

```{r}
Ls <- matrix(NA, nrow=N, ncol=length(K$border))
for(i in 1:N){
  # draw from random sample
  x_rand <- runif(nrow(test_df), min(test_df$x), max(test_df$x))
  y_rand <- runif(nrow(test_df), min(test_df$y), max(test_df$y))
  tmp_df <- data.frame(x=x_rand, y=y_rand)
  p_tmp <- ppp(tmp_df$x, tmp_df$y, owin(range(tmp_df$x), range(tmp_df$y)))
  # p_tmp <- ppp(tmp_df$x, tmp_df$y, owin(xrange, yrange))
  tmpK <- Kest(p_tmp)
  tmpL <- sqrt(tmpK$border / pi) - tmpK$r
  Ls[i, ] <- tmpL
  # Ks[i, ] <- tmpK$border
}

Ls_max <- apply(Ls, 2, max, na.rm=T)
Ls_min <- apply(Ls, 2, min, na.rm=T)
```

# plot(p_env$r, rep(NA, length(p_env$r)), ylim=ylim, type="n", xlab="r", ylab="L(r)")
# points(p_env$r, sqrt(p_env$obs / pi) - p_env$r, type="l", lty=1, col=1)
# points(p_env$r, sqrt(p_env$theo / pi) - p_env$r, type="l", lty=2, col=4)
# points(p_env$r, sqrt(p_env$hi / pi) - p_env$r, type="l", lty=2, col=2)
# points(p_env$r, sqrt(p_env$lo / pi) - p_env$r, type="l", lty=2, col=2)

```{r}
layout(matrix(1:2, nrow=1))
# plot the point pattern
plot(test_df$x, test_df$y, pch=16, col=point_col, xlab="x", ylab="y")
# plot the Ripley's K w/ CI
ylim <- c(min(c(L, Ls_max, Ls_min), na.rm=T), max(c(L, Ls_max, Ls_min), na.rm=T))
plot(K$r, L, lwd=2, col=1, ylim=ylim, type="l", xlab="d", ylab="L(d)-d")
points(K$r, Ls_max, type="l", lty=3, col=2)
points(K$r, Ls_min, type="l", lty=3, col=2)
legend("topleft", legend=c("Lobs", "99% CI"), lty=c(1,2), col=c(1,2), lwd=c(2, 1))
```


#----------------------------------------------------------------
# bivariate
```{r}
# now working with longleaf pine data 
layout(matrix(1:2, nrow=1))
plot(longleaf)
point_col1 <- rgb(matrix(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Blues")[5]) / 255, ncol=3), alpha=0.5)
point_col2 <- rgb(matrix(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Reds")[5]) / 255, ncol=3), alpha=0.5)
plot(NA, xlim=range(longleaf$x), ylim=range(longleaf$y), xlab="", ylab="")
points(longleaf[marks(longleaf) <= 15], pch=16, col=point_col1)
points(longleaf[marks(longleaf) >= 25], pch=16, col=point_col2)
legend("bottom", legend=c("<=15", ">=25"), pch=16, col=c(point_col1, point_col2), horiz=T, bg="white")
```
```{r}
# plot univariate and bivariate K functions for small and large trees
layout(matrix(1:3, nrow=1))
plot(Kest(longleaf[marks(longleaf) <= 15]))
plot(Kest(longleaf[marks(longleaf) >= 25]))
plot(Kmulti(longleaf, marks(longleaf) <=15, marks(longleaf) >=25))
# The univariate pattern for juveniles is above the poisson - means it's clustered
# adult trees are clustered but to a lesser extent 
# shows a pattern of replusion between adult and juvenile trees
```
```{r}
# bootstrap CI
N <- 100
# The results of the thing we did earlier
K_trees <- Kmulti(longleaf, marks(longleaf) <=15, marks(longleaf) >=25)
# convert to L so that we have the 0 expectation
L_trees <- sqrt(K_trees$border / pi) - K_trees$r
# preallocating our space in the matrix 
Ls <- matrix(NA, nrow=N, ncol=length(K_trees$r))
for(i in 1:N){
  # do label permutation
  # sampling the marks to define the i group and the j group 
  K_tmp <- Kmulti(longleaf, sample(marks(longleaf) <= 15), sample(marks(longleaf) >= 25))
  L_tmp <- sqrt(K_tmp$border / pi) - K_tmp$r
  Ls[i, ] <- L_tmp
}
```


```{r}
Ls_min <- apply(Ls, 2, min)
Ls_max <- apply(Ls, 2, max)
```


```{r}
ylim <- c(min(c(L_trees, Ls_max, Ls_min), na.rm=T), max(c(L_trees, Ls_max, Ls_min), na.rm=T))
plot(K_trees$r, L_trees, lwd=2, col=1, ylim=ylim, type="l", xlab="d", ylab="L(d)-d")
points(K_trees$r, Ls_max, type="l", lty=3, col=2)
points(K_trees$r, Ls_min, type="l", lty=3, col=2)
legend("topleft", legend=c("Lobs", "99% CI"), lty=c(1,2), col=c(1,2), lwd=c(2, 1))
# all of the k values are outside the confidence interval 
# around every adult tree are fewer juveniles than you would expect 
```
